perplexity.description:
Released in 1977 on Bearsville Records, Ra is the second studio album by the American rock band Utopia, led by Todd Rundgren. Musically, the album reflects the group's progressive rock roots, opening with an electronic arrangement of Bernard Herrmann's "Overture: Mountaintop and Sunrise" from the film Journey to the Center of the Earth. This ambitious, multi-part suite sets the tone for an album that blends intricate instrumentation, experimental textures, and conceptual themes, while also incorporating shorter, more accessible tracks that hint at the pop-oriented direction Utopia would later pursue.

Ra occupies a transitional place in Utopia's discography, marking the last album before the band began shifting toward a more concise, new wave-influenced sound. It reached number 79 on the US Billboard 200 and number 27 on the UK Albums Chart, indicating moderate commercial success. Critics generally recognized the album's progressive leanings and technical proficiency, though its eclectic mix of styles drew varied responses. Ra remains a notable entry in Utopia's catalog for its ambitious scope and its role in the band's evolution from progressive rock toward pop.
